data.narrative:
DefSecIntel, a Series A-stage company in Defense & Security founded by Jaanus Tamm, is evaluated against a comparable universe of 11 same-sector and adjacent-stage peers, comprising 2 public companies and 8 private firms. Key private comparables include Singularity, NODA AI, Anduril Industries, Helsing, and Castelion, with public references DRSHF and IDEAFORGE.NS.

Peer-median valuation analysis anchors the primary valuation method. The median across the 11-company peer set stands at $1.0B, with a range spanning $125M at the low end to $3.0B at the high end. Within the sample, Dream Security is valued at $3.0B (Series B), Allen Control Systems at $2.2B (Series B), Harmattan AI at $1.4B (Series B), Code Metal at $1.2B (Series B), and Twenty at $1.0B (Series B), establishing substantial precedent for defensible valuations in this segment.

The triangulated valuation range is $850M to $1.1B, with a median of $1.0B. This analysis relies on a single method—peer-median comparison—reflecting the limited applicability of revenue multiples or DCF approaches given typical Series A-stage data constraints. Key uncertainties center on DefSecIntel's relative competitive positioning, customer concentration, and revenue trajectory relative to the peer set, all material to justifying placement within this range.
